# Block reference

One section per block type, from `nagasim/core/block_registry.py`. Types marked *editor-only* never run: the engine flattens them away before a run.

## ASSIGN

Sets attributes on a part, order or customer, or a model variable, from expressions as it passes, for example a due date, a type or a counter. Takes an ordered list of assignments, each is `{"target": "entity.<attr>" | "entity.agent.<attr>" | "<variable>", "expr": "<expression>"}`. Assignments run in order, so a later one sees what an earlier one wrote. Targets and expressions both go through core/expressions.py -- a model file never executes Python.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assignments` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Ordered list of {"target": "entity.<attr>" | "entity.agent.<attr>" | "<variable>", "expr": "<expression>"}; each runs in order. |

Outputs: 1.

## BATCH

Groups parts or orders into batches, pallets or lots of a set size, or after a maximum wait, and sends the batch on as one entity. Groups entities by count: puts each arrival in the block's store and, as soon as `batch_size` items are waiting, takes exactly that many atomically to form one batch entity. Members leave live_entities and carry `in_batch` until a SEPARATE splits the batch again. With `max_wait` set, a PARTIAL batch leaves too: the timer is armed by the arrival that starts a new group and releases whatever is waiting once the oldest member has waited that long. TIE RULE: a batch that fills in the same instant as the timer expires wins and the timer releases nothing -- the same zero-delay re-check reneging uses, so the outcome never depends on the order SimPy happened to schedule two events at one timestamp. With `carrier_type` set, an arrival of that type is a CARRIER (a truck): it is not stored, and loads the stored arrivals one at a time, `member_time` each, until it holds `carrier_capacity` (default `batch_size`) or its `max_wait`, counted from its own arrival, has passed; then it leaves as itself, its members aboard.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_size` | int | `2` |  | count |  | Number of entities grouped into one batch entity. |
| `batched_entity_type` | str | `'BATCH'` |  |  |  | Entity type assigned to the batch entity. |
| `max_wait` | str | `''` |  | time | `max_wait_time_unit` | How long a partial batch waits before it leaves anyway, e.g. "30" or "entity.deadline"; measured from the arrival that started the group. A batch that fills in the same instant wins. Empty, 0 or less = wait for a full batch for ever. |
| `max_wait_time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit `max_wait` is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `carrier_type` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Carrier mode: an arriving entity of this type (a truck) is a CARRIER that waits here and loads the other arrivals one at a time, until it is full or its max_wait (the cut-off, measured from the carrier's arrival) runs out, then leaves as itself. Empty = a plain BATCH. |
| `carrier_capacity` | str | `''` |  | count |  | Carrier mode: how many members a carrier takes, e.g. "entity.capacity", evaluated for each carrier when it arrives. Empty = batch_size. |
| `member_time` | str | `''` |  | time | `member_time_unit` | Carrier mode: time to load one member, evaluated in the member's own scope when its load starts. Empty = loading takes no time. |
| `member_time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit `member_time` is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |

Outputs: 1.

## BUFFER

Finite storage of waiting places between two machines or stations; when all places are taken the upstream machine stays blocked, holding its finished part.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `capacity` | int | `1` | yes | count |  | Places in the buffer, 0 or more. A part takes one on the way in and holds it until the next station accepts it, so an upstream machine blocks while the buffer is full. 0 means no place at all (blocking after service with no buffer); for an unlimited queue, do not draw a buffer. |
| `level` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Optional level whose value mirrors the buffer's content, so an asset can draw it as a fill indicator. Empty = no level. |

Outputs: 1.

## CHARGE

Charges an entity (an electric vehicle, a battery pack) with the energy it needs at up to its own power, sharing a site power cap with every other entity at this block; it leaves when full or when its time is up. The block's total grid kW (what the entities take over `efficiency`) is kept in `power_variable`, so a flow with `rate: VAR("name")` puts it on the electricity bus; `site_limit` caps that grid kW. On leaving the entity carries `charged_kwh`, `charge_full` (1 or 0) and `charge_time` (entry to full, or to leaving when not full, in `time_limit_unit`).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `energy` | str | `'0'` | yes | energy |  | Energy the entity needs, kWh: an expression, e.g. entity.need_kwh. |
| `max_power` | str | `'0'` | yes | power |  | Most power the entity takes, kW: an expression, e.g. min(11, entity.max_kw). |
| `time_limit` | str | `''` |  | time | `time_limit_unit` | Longest time the entity stays (an expression); it leaves then, full or not. Empty = until full. |
| `time_limit_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `time_limit` and of the `charge_time` the entity carries: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |
| `time_limit_from` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Instant, in model time, the time limit counts from: an expression such as entity.arrived_at. Empty = when the entity enters. A deadline already past sends it on at once, charged 0. |
| `leave_when_full` | bool | `True` |  |  |  | Leave as soon as the need is met. Off: stay (drawing nothing) until the time limit, as a car stays plugged in. |
| `site_limit` | float | `0.0` |  | power |  | Most power all entities at this block draw together from the grid, kW; 0 = no cap. |
| `efficiency` | float | `1.0` |  | ratio |  | Energy the entity stores per unit drawn from the grid (charger losses); 1 = none. The site limit and power_variable are grid side. |
| `sharing` | str | `'equal'` |  |  |  | How the cap is shared: "equal" (an equal share each; what a slow entity cannot use goes to the others) or "first_come" (in order of arrival, each as much as it can take). |
| `power_variable` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Model variable kept equal to the block's total grid kW, for a flow rate VAR("name") on the electricity bus. Empty = none. |

Outputs: 1.

## CONVEYOR

Conveyor belt that carries parts from one end to the other at a set speed, holds a limited number, and blocks the machine before it when full.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | float | `0.0` |  | length | `length_unit` | Belt length in layout units. 0 takes the network distance between `from_node` and `to_node`. |
| `length_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `length`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |
| `speed` | float | `1.0` | yes | speed | `speed_unit` | Belt speed, length units per model time unit. |
| `speed_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `speed`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |
| `spacing` | float | `1.0` | yes | length | `spacing_unit` | Belt length one entity occupies; capacity is floor(length / spacing) and the entry rhythm is spacing / speed. |
| `spacing_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `spacing`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |
| `accumulating` | bool | `True` |  |  |  | True: a blocked entity stops and the others pack behind it. False: the whole belt stops while the exit is blocked. |
| `exit_resource` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Resource an entity must take to leave the belt -- the end stop that makes accumulation happen. It carries the resource onward, so release it downstream (a PROCESS with action "Delay Release"). Empty: no end stop. Either way, a belt that feeds another belt keeps its end part until that belt has room (back-pressure). |
| `from_node` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Path-network node the belt starts at (drawing, and the length when `length` is 0). |
| `to_node` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Path-network node the belt ends at. |
| `stops` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Points where each part halts on the belt: {"at": <distance from the entry, in the unit of `length`, between 0 and the length>, "time": <number or expression>, "resource"?: <seized for the stop>}. Parts behind pack against a stop on an accumulating belt; a non-accumulating belt stops while a part is at one. Empty: none. |
| `diverts` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Points where a part may leave the belt sideways: {"at": <distance from the entry, in the unit of `length`>, "condition": <expression, read once as the part reaches it>, "time"?: <push time, number or expression>, "when_full"?: "wait" (default: the part waits there for room) or "pass" (it rides on)}. Divert k leaves by outgoing link k + 1; link 0 is the belt's end. Empty: none. |
| `merges` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Points where parts from another block join the belt: {"at": <distance from the entry, in the unit of `length`>, "from": <the block linking to this belt whose parts join there>, "priority"?: "belt" (default: they wait for a gap of two spacings) or "merge" (parts on the belt make room)}. Accumulating belts only. Empty: none. |

Outputs: 1.

## CREATE

Source of arrivals: creates parts, orders, customers or jobs at random intervals or on an hourly arrival schedule. Either samples the inter-arrival gap from `distribution` (`arrival_mode = "Interarrival"`, the classic behaviour) or drives a non-homogeneous Poisson process from an arrival `Schedule` by thinning (`arrival_mode = "Schedule"`). Every model needs at least one CREATE block.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `e_type` | str | `'DEFAULT'` |  |  |  | Entity type assigned to every entity this block creates. |
| `arrival_mode` | str | `'Interarrival'` |  |  |  | "Interarrival": sample the gap from `distribution`. "Schedule": a non-homogeneous Poisson process driven by `schedule_name`. "Orders": release the model's declared orders, each at its own release time with its due date, quantity and routing. |
| `schedule_name` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of an arrival Schedule to drive from, when arrival_mode is "Schedule". |
| `distribution` | str | `'Constant'` |  |  |  | Name of a registered distribution (see the distribution reference). |
| `dist_params` | dict | `{'value': 1.0}` |  | time | `time_unit` | Parameters for `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). |
| `time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit the sampled duration is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit, no conversion) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `entities_per_arrival` | int | `1` |  | count |  | Number of entities created per arrival event. |
| `max_arrivals` | int | `0` |  | count |  | Number of arrival events before this block stops; 0 = unlimited. |
| `start_time` | float | `0` |  | time | `start_time_unit` | Simulation time of the first possible arrival. |
| `start_time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `start_time`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |
| `sequence` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of a declared routing sequence: every entity created here starts it at step 0. Empty = no routing. It is a literal name, not an expression -- use an ASSIGN to entity.sequence when the routing depends on the entity. |
| `population` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of a declared population. When set, every entity created here also gets a new agent there (its statechart starts), and entity.agent points to it. Empty = off. A full population raises the same error a spawn action would. |

Outputs: 1.

## DECIDE

Routing decision: sends each part, order or customer down one of several links by percentage chance, by a condition (rework, type, size) or by a policy. "Chance" mode draws on the block's own RNG against cumulative `probs`; "Condition" mode evaluates each of `conditions` in order and takes the first true one. Both modes take the last outgoing link as an ELSE branch when there is one more link than probs/conditions; otherwise an uncovered draw or condition fails loud rather than silently dropping the entity. "Policy" mode hands the choice to `ctx.controllers[policy]`: the number of actions is simply the number of outgoing links. A plain (synchronous) controller is called inline, in zero simulated time, exactly like Chance/Condition above. A `PausingController` (used by `nagasim.rl. SimEnv` to drive the policy from outside the run) is different: this block yields on a simpy event instead, so the whole simulation genuinely pauses until something resolves it. With no controller attached for `policy`, the block falls back to `fallback` ("first" / "random" / "shortest") so a Policy-mode model still runs and validates headless.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | str | `'Chance'` |  |  |  | "Chance": branch by probability. "Condition": branch by expression. "Policy": branch by a controller attached to `policy`. |
| `probs` | list | `[]` |  | ratio |  | Cumulative branch probabilities, used when mode is "Chance". |
| `conditions` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Ordered list of boolean expressions, used when mode is "Condition". |
| `policy` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Decision-point name; used when mode is "Policy". Several DECIDE blocks may share one. |
| `observation` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Expressions (evaluated with the arriving entity) forming the observation handed to the controller, when mode is "Policy". |
| `fallback` | str | `'first'` |  |  |  | "first"/"random"/"shortest": used when mode is "Policy" and no controller is attached for `policy`. |
| `queue_exprs` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | One expression per outgoing link; used by fallback "shortest" to pick the argmin. |

Outputs: multiple, chosen at run time.

## DELAY

Pure waiting time (transit, curing, travel, a pause) that holds the entity for a sampled duration without using any machine, operator or other resource. Seizes nothing, then forwards it. Use PROCESS instead when the delay is a resource-backed service.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `distribution` | str | `'Constant'` |  |  |  | Name of a registered distribution (see the distribution reference). |
| `dist_params` | dict | `{'value': 0.0}` |  | time | `time_unit` | Parameters for `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). |
| `time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit the sampled duration is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit, no conversion) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |

Outputs: 1.

## DISPOSE

End of the flow: parts, orders or customers leave the system here, and their throughput time and holding cost are recorded. Waits an optional deletion delay, stamps deletion_time and throughput_time, accrues the entity type's WIP holding cost, and removes the entity from live_entities. Every model needs at least one DISPOSE block, and every flow that does not lead back to a CREATE must end in one (schema.validate_graph_structured).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `distribution` | str | `'Constant'` |  |  |  | Name of a registered distribution (see the distribution reference). |
| `dist_params` | dict | `{'value': 0.0}` |  | time | `time_unit` | Parameters for `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). |
| `time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit the sampled duration is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit, no conversion) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `remove_agent` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | When true, also remove the entity's agent (AgentSystem.remove_agent) at disposal, if it still has a live one. An entity with none, or whose agent already died, is a no-op. |

Outputs: 1.

## DUPLICATE

Makes copies of an entity, for example to send the same order to several branches or to model one job spawning several; the original goes on unchanged. Forwards the original entity unchanged, then forwards `number_of_duplicates - 1` shallow copies, each a fresh Entity with its own id and name (never a deepcopy: that used to clone the entity manager and any live resource requests).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `number_of_duplicates` | int | `2` |  | count |  | Total number of entities leaving this block, original included (>= 2). |

Outputs: 1.

## HOLD

Holds entities waiting in a queue until a named signal fires, a condition becomes true (a buffer has room, a machine is idle), or for good. Infinite mode never releases: the entity stays held in the store for the rest of the run. That is the documented semantics, not a leak.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | str | `'Signal'` |  |  |  | "Signal": wait for a named signal. "Condition": wait until every condition is true, re-checked whenever something it reads changes. "Infinite": never release. |
| `signal_name` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of the signal to wait for, when mode is "Signal". |
| `conditions` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Boolean expressions that must all be true to release, when mode is "Condition". |
| `scan_interval` | float | `1.0` |  | time | `scan_interval_unit` | Fallback re-check interval, when mode is "Condition": used only when a condition reads something no event announces (TNOW, TS(), RAND(), a level between events). Variables, NQ/NR/MR/IDLE, NS and threshold writes wake it at once. |
| `scan_interval_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `scan_interval`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |

Outputs: 1.

## LOGIC

Custom routing written in Python: sends each entity to one of several outgoing links by your own rule when chance or a condition is not enough. Routes an entity through a user-supplied, plain (non-BaseProcess) class defined in nagasim.core.custom_logic. The class only needs an `execute(self, entity, ctx) -> int` method returning the outgoing link index; `execute(self, entity)` (no ctx) is also accepted.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `logic_class` | str | `'SampleLogic'` |  |  |  | Name of a class in nagasim.core.custom_logic implementing execute(entity, ctx) -> int. |

Outputs: multiple, chosen at run time.

## MATCH

Waits until one entity of each of several kinds is present (a part and its kit, an order and its customer), then releases them together. Match `number_to_match` *distinct* entity types; with `match_on` set, only entities whose value of that attribute is equal (Arena's attribute match). The arriving entity is always stored first, so it can never be dropped ; the match is then taken atomically from the stores, oldest waiting type first, FIFO within a type (and within a value).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `number_to_match` | int | `2` |  | count |  | Number of distinct entity types to match together. |
| `batch_option` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | True: combine the matched entities into one batch entity. False: forward them separately. |
| `batched_entity_type` | str | `'BATCH'` |  |  |  | Entity type assigned to the batch entity, when batch_option is True. |
| `type_store_map` | dict | `{}` |  |  |  | Optional {e_type: store index} mapping; default is automatic assignment. |
| `match_on` | str | `''` |  |  |  | An entity attribute (e.g. "order"); entities are matched only with others whose value of it is equal -- Arena's attribute match -- still one per distinct type, FIFO within a value. Empty = match by type alone. |

Outputs: 1.

## MOTION

Robot or cobot station whose service is a cycle of timed moves, picks, places and tool changes, so cycle time comes from motion data, not a distribution. A station whose service is a cycle of motions -- moves timed from a motion profile (trapezoidal, payload-derated, slowed for human-robot collaboration) plus picks, places, tool changes, dwells and process steps. Seizing, setups, failures, preemption, workers and blocking are PROCESS's.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | str | `'Seize Delay Release'` |  |  |  | Which of seize/delay/release run: "Seize Delay Release", "Seize Delay", "Delay Release" or "Delay". |
| `profile` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of a record in "motion_profiles": speed, acceleration, payload derating and collaborative speed of whoever does the motions. |
| `hrc` | str | `'none'` |  |  |  | Human-robot collaboration: "none", "collaborative" (every move at the profile's collaborative_speed) or "separation" (a move starts at collaborative_speed when a worker-fleet unit is within the zone's radius of its node, by path or straight distance). |
| `zone` | dict | `{}` |  |  |  | With hrc "separation": {"name": <a "zones" record>} -- the record's node and radius win -- or, with no name, {"node": <network node>, "radius_m": <metres>, "measure"?: "path"|"straight"}. |
| `segments` | list | `[]` |  | time | `time_unit` | The cycle, in order: {"kind": "move", "distance_m", "payload_kg"?} or {"kind": pick|place|tool_change|dwell|process, "time": <number or expression>}. The service time is their sum. |
| `time_unit` | str | `'seconds'` |  |  |  | Unit of every segment `time`: "base" or seconds/minutes/hours/days. Moves are always computed in seconds. |
| `priority` | int | `0` |  |  |  | Lower draws first when the resource's queue is contested. One number for the block (an entity attribute is not read): to rank entity types, route each to its own block on the shared resource. |
| `quantity` | int | `1` |  | count |  | Number of resource units requested/released. |
| `resource_name` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of the resource or resource set; required unless action is "Delay" or a worker_fleet does the work alone. |
| `setup` | str | `''` |  | time | `setup_unit` | Sequence-dependent setup time: an expression charged after the seize when this block's resource changes over, e.g. TABLE("Setups", previous_key, key). `previous_key` and `key` are in scope here only. Empty = no setup. |
| `setup_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `setup`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |
| `setup_key` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Expression identifying what a job is set up for; empty uses the entity type. A setup is charged only when it differs from the previous job's key at this block. |
| `initial_key` | str | `''` |  |  |  | What the resource is already set up for at time 0; empty means the first job is charged no setup. |
| `setup_cost` | str | `''` |  | money |  | Money charged ONCE PER CHANGEOVER, not per job -- an expression like TABLE("Changeover cost", previous_key, key), with `previous_key` and `key` in scope exactly as in "setup". It becomes an event cost item named after the block, joins Total Cost and resets at warm-up. Empty = free changeovers. |
| `setup_cost_category` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Cost category the changeover cost is grouped under in the cost_summary frame (default "Changeover"). |
| `balk_if` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Condition evaluated on arrival; when true the entity does not join the queue and leaves by the second outgoing link, e.g. "queue_length >= 5". `queue_length` is the queue it would have joined. Empty = never balk. |
| `renege_after` | str | `''` |  | time | `renege_time_unit` | How long the entity waits before giving up, e.g. "EXPO(15)" or "entity.patience"; it then leaves by the second outgoing link. A grant in the same instant wins. Empty = wait for ever. |
| `renege_time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit `renege_after` is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `preempt` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | When no unit is free, interrupt the lowest-priority job in service on this resource (a strictly higher priority wins). Only with action "Seize Delay Release", and not on a resource set. |
| `queue_capacity` | int | `0` |  | count |  | Places in this station's own input queue. 0 (the default) is an unlimited queue; with a positive value a part takes a place on arrival and frees it when service starts, so an upstream machine with nowhere to put its finished part stays blocked. `balk_if` sees the places taken as `queue_length`, which is how a LOSS system is written instead of a blocking one. |
| `hold_until_space` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | Blocking BEFORE service: after seizing, do not start the job until the downstream space has a free place, and reserve it for this part. The station waits idle (reported as Blocked %). Needs a downstream BUFFER with capacity > 0 or a SEIZE/PROCESS with queue_capacity > 0. Off (the default) is blocking AFTER service. |
| `space_of` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Which block's space `hold_until_space` reserves in; empty = the target of this block's first outgoing link. The part must reach that block. |
| `worker_fleet` | str | `''` |  |  |  | A fleet with kind "worker". After this block's own resource (if any) is seized, a worker is requested, walks EMPTY on the network to `node`, and is held for the service. Empty = no worker. |
| `worker_skill` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Only a worker whose skills contain this name may serve; empty = any worker of the fleet. |
| `node` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Network node this block sits on; required with worker_fleet (where the worker walks to). |
| `worker_when_blocked` | str | `'leaves'` |  |  |  | What the worker does while this station holds a finished part that nothing downstream has room for. "leaves" (the default): the worker is free when the work ends. "stays": the worker waits with the part and is free when it is accepted downstream. The same either way where nothing downstream is finite. |
| `on_preempt` | str | `'resume'` |  |  |  | What THIS block's job does when something interrupts it and it gets the resource back: "resume" (finish the remaining time) or "restart" (the whole service again, same sample). Set on the block being interrupted, not on the one doing the interrupting. |
| `resample` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | With on_preempt "restart" only: draw a FRESH service time from this block's own random stream on each restart, instead of repeating the same sample. Off (the default) repeats it. |

Outputs: 1.

## PROCESS

Machine, workstation or service step: a part, order or customer waits for a resource (machine, operator, server), is processed for a time, then frees it. Seize, delay and release fused in one block; `action` selects which of the three steps run ("Seize Delay Release", "Seize Delay", "Delay Release", "Delay"), so the same block type covers a self-contained service, the start or end of a hold split across two blocks, or a plain timed delay. The most-used block for a simple resource-backed service step.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | str | `'Seize Delay Release'` |  |  |  | Which of seize/delay/release run: "Seize Delay Release", "Seize Delay", "Delay Release" or "Delay". |
| `distribution` | str | `'Constant'` |  |  |  | Name of a registered distribution (see the distribution reference). |
| `dist_params` | dict | `{'value': 0.0}` |  | time | `time_unit` | Parameters for `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). |
| `time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit the sampled duration is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit, no conversion) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `priority` | int | `0` |  |  |  | Lower draws first when the resource's queue is contested. One number for the block (an entity attribute is not read): to rank entity types, route each to its own block on the shared resource. |
| `quantity` | int | `1` |  | count |  | Number of resource units requested/released. |
| `resource_name` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of the resource or resource set; required unless action is "Delay" or a worker_fleet does the work alone. |
| `setup` | str | `''` |  | time | `setup_unit` | Sequence-dependent setup time: an expression charged after the seize when this block's resource changes over, e.g. TABLE("Setups", previous_key, key). `previous_key` and `key` are in scope here only. Empty = no setup. |
| `setup_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `setup`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |
| `setup_key` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Expression identifying what a job is set up for; empty uses the entity type. A setup is charged only when it differs from the previous job's key at this block. |
| `initial_key` | str | `''` |  |  |  | What the resource is already set up for at time 0; empty means the first job is charged no setup. |
| `setup_cost` | str | `''` |  | money |  | Money charged ONCE PER CHANGEOVER, not per job -- an expression like TABLE("Changeover cost", previous_key, key), with `previous_key` and `key` in scope exactly as in "setup". It becomes an event cost item named after the block, joins Total Cost and resets at warm-up. Empty = free changeovers. |
| `setup_cost_category` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Cost category the changeover cost is grouped under in the cost_summary frame (default "Changeover"). |
| `balk_if` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Condition evaluated on arrival; when true the entity does not join the queue and leaves by the second outgoing link, e.g. "queue_length >= 5". `queue_length` is the queue it would have joined. Empty = never balk. |
| `renege_after` | str | `''` |  | time | `renege_time_unit` | How long the entity waits before giving up, e.g. "EXPO(15)" or "entity.patience"; it then leaves by the second outgoing link. A grant in the same instant wins. Empty = wait for ever. |
| `renege_time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit `renege_after` is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `preempt` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | When no unit is free, interrupt the lowest-priority job in service on this resource (a strictly higher priority wins). Only with action "Seize Delay Release", and not on a resource set. |
| `queue_capacity` | int | `0` |  | count |  | Places in this station's own input queue. 0 (the default) is an unlimited queue; with a positive value a part takes a place on arrival and frees it when service starts, so an upstream machine with nowhere to put its finished part stays blocked. `balk_if` sees the places taken as `queue_length`, which is how a LOSS system is written instead of a blocking one. |
| `hold_until_space` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | Blocking BEFORE service: after seizing, do not start the job until the downstream space has a free place, and reserve it for this part. The station waits idle (reported as Blocked %). Needs a downstream BUFFER with capacity > 0 or a SEIZE/PROCESS with queue_capacity > 0. Off (the default) is blocking AFTER service. |
| `space_of` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Which block's space `hold_until_space` reserves in; empty = the target of this block's first outgoing link. The part must reach that block. |
| `worker_fleet` | str | `''` |  |  |  | A fleet with kind "worker". After this block's own resource (if any) is seized, a worker is requested, walks EMPTY on the network to `node`, and is held for the service. Empty = no worker. |
| `worker_skill` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Only a worker whose skills contain this name may serve; empty = any worker of the fleet. |
| `node` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Network node this block sits on; required with worker_fleet (where the worker walks to). |
| `worker_when_blocked` | str | `'leaves'` |  |  |  | What the worker does while this station holds a finished part that nothing downstream has room for. "leaves" (the default): the worker is free when the work ends. "stays": the worker waits with the part and is free when it is accepted downstream. The same either way where nothing downstream is finite. |
| `on_preempt` | str | `'resume'` |  |  |  | What THIS block's job does when something interrupts it and it gets the resource back: "resume" (finish the remaining time) or "restart" (the whole service again, same sample). Set on the block being interrupted, not on the one doing the interrupting. |
| `resample` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | With on_preempt "restart" only: draw a FRESH service time from this block's own random stream on each restart, instead of repeating the same sample. Off (the default) repeats it. |

Outputs: 1.

## RECORD

Counts or measures something as entities pass (a count, a time between arrivals, a defect, a cost) in a user-named statistic, without delaying them. A zero-time block that updates a user-defined statistic and forwards the entity unchanged. Statistics live on the simulation context (`ctx.user_stats`), keyed by `stat_name`, so two RECORD blocks writing to the same name share one collector -- core/schema/ rejects a same-name pair with different `kind`s at load time, before a run can hit the mismatch here. `expr` is the increment for "count", the observed value for "tally", the new level for "time_persistent", and ignored for "time_between" (it tallies the gap since the statistic's last arrival; the first arrival records nothing). `kind="cost"` is the one kind that builds no collector: `expr` is a MONEY amount added to the cost item `stat_name` every time an entity passes -- an ordering cost, a changeover cost, a lost-sale penalty. It joins the model's Total Cost and is itemised in the `cost_summary` frame.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stat_name` | str | `''` | yes |  |  | Name of the user statistic; two RECORD blocks with the same name share one collector. |
| `kind` | str | `'count'` |  |  |  | "count" (running total of expr), "tally" (mean of expr), "time_between" (mean gap between arrivals), "time_persistent" (time-average level of expr) or "cost" (adds expr to a named cost item and to Total Cost). |
| `expr` | str | `'1'` |  |  |  | Expression evaluated at each arrival; ignored for kind=time_between. |
| `category` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Cost category this item is grouped under in the cost_summary frame; used by kind=cost only. |

Outputs: 1.

## RELEASE

Frees a machine, operator or other resource that an earlier SEIZE gave the entity, after an optional delay. Release everything the entity holds under `resource_name` (a plain resource or a set member), after an optional delay. Pairs with SEIZE for a hold split across two blocks; raises if the entity never seized that name (fail-loud by design).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `distribution` | str | `'Constant'` |  |  |  | Name of a registered distribution (see the distribution reference). |
| `dist_params` | dict | `{'value': 0.0}` |  | time | `time_unit` | Parameters for `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). |
| `time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit the sampled duration is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit, no conversion) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `resource_name` | str | `''` | yes |  |  | Name of the resource or resource set to release. |
| `worker_when_blocked` | str | `'leaves'` |  |  |  | What the worker does while this station holds a finished part that nothing downstream has room for. "leaves" (the default): the worker is free when the work ends. "stays": the worker waits with the part and is free when it is accepted downstream. The same either way where nothing downstream is finite. |

Outputs: 1.

## ROUTE

Sends a part or job to the next station on its own routing sequence (a job-shop or multi-step route) instead of along a fixed link. Send the entity to the next station of its `sequence`, applying that step's attribute values and advancing its `step` index; once the sequence is finished, forward along the block's own outgoing link instead.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `distribution` | str | `'Constant'` |  |  |  | Name of a registered distribution (see the distribution reference). |
| `dist_params` | dict | `{'value': 0.0}` |  | time | `time_unit` | Parameters for `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). |
| `time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit the sampled duration is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit, no conversion) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `travel` | str | `'time'` |  |  |  | How the transfer time is found: "time" uses the distribution above, "network" divides the shortest path between the two stations' nodes by `speed`. |
| `speed` | str | `''` |  | speed | `speed_unit` | Travel speed for `travel = "network"`, an expression in distance per time unit (e.g. 1.2, or `entity.walk_speed`). Empty means 1. |
| `speed_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `speed`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |

Outputs: 1.

## SEIZE

Waits in a queue for a machine, operator, vehicle or other resource, takes it and keeps it until a later RELEASE, so one resource can span several steps. Request `quantity` units of `resource_name` (a plain resource or a resource set), honouring priority and the resource's queue discipline, then hold the block's own delay before forwarding. Pairs with RELEASE for a hold split across two blocks; PROCESS fuses the common Seize-Delay- Release case into one block. `balk_if` and `renege_after` let an entity leave without ever being served, by the block's second outgoing link. Preemption is PROCESS only: the service a SEIZE starts is finished somewhere else, so there is nothing here that could safely be interrupted.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `distribution` | str | `'Constant'` |  |  |  | Name of a registered distribution (see the distribution reference). |
| `dist_params` | dict | `{'value': 0.0}` |  | time | `time_unit` | Parameters for `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). |
| `time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit the sampled duration is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit, no conversion) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `priority` | int | `0` |  |  |  | Lower draws first when the resource's queue is contested. One number for the block (an entity attribute is not read): to rank entity types, route each to its own block on the shared resource. |
| `quantity` | int | `1` |  | count |  | Number of resource units requested. |
| `resource_name` | str | `''` | yes |  |  | Name of the resource or resource set to seize. |
| `queue_capacity` | int | `0` |  | count |  | Places in this block's own input queue. 0 (the default) is an unlimited queue; with a positive value a part takes a place on arrival and frees it when it seizes, so an upstream machine with nowhere to put its finished part stays blocked. |
| `hold_until_space` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | Blocking BEFORE service: after seizing, do not start the job until the downstream space has a free place, and reserve it for this part. The station waits idle (reported as Blocked %). Needs a downstream BUFFER with capacity > 0 or a SEIZE/PROCESS with queue_capacity > 0. Off (the default) is blocking AFTER service. |
| `space_of` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Which block's space `hold_until_space` reserves in; empty = the target of this block's first outgoing link. The part must reach that block. |
| `worker_fleet` | str | `''` |  |  |  | A fleet with kind "worker". After this block's own resource (if any) is seized, a worker is requested, walks EMPTY on the network to `node`, and is held for the service. Empty = no worker. |
| `worker_skill` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Only a worker whose skills contain this name may serve; empty = any worker of the fleet. |
| `node` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Network node this block sits on; required with worker_fleet (where the worker walks to). |
| `balk_if` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Condition evaluated on arrival; when true the entity does not join the queue and leaves by the second outgoing link, e.g. "queue_length >= 5". `queue_length` is the queue it would have joined. Empty = never balk. |
| `renege_after` | str | `''` |  | time | `renege_time_unit` | How long the entity waits before giving up, e.g. "EXPO(15)" or "entity.patience"; it then leaves by the second outgoing link. A grant in the same instant wins. Empty = wait for ever. |
| `renege_time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit `renege_after` is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |

Outputs: 1.

## SEND

Sends a message, with an optional payload, to agents of an agent-based model so they can react, for example a customer calling a driver.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | str | `''` | yes |  |  | Name of the message; an agent's "message" transition matches it. |
| `to` | object | `'entity.agent'` |  |  |  | Recipients: an expression giving an agent (entity.agent, AGENT("Pop", i)) or {"population": "Pop"[, "where": "<condition on self>"]\[, "random": true]}. |
| `payload` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Optional expression evaluated for the entity; the receiving transition reads it as `payload`. |

Outputs: 1.

## SEPARATE

Splits a batch, pallet or lot back into its individual parts, orders or customers, optionally copying the batch's attributes to each. Parameters ---------- mode : {'retain','all','specific'} - 'retain' children keep their own attributes - 'all' copy *all* parent attributes to each child - 'specific' copy only the names listed in *attrs* attrs : list[str] | str | None Comma-separated string or list used when *mode* == 'specific'. carrier : {'dispose','keep'} 'keep': the parent is a CARRIER (a truck) that lives on. Its members leave one at a time on exit 0, each after its own `member_time`, and the carrier leaves on exit 1 once it is empty.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | str | `'Retain original entity values'` |  |  |  | How children get their attributes: retain their own values, take all of the parent's, or take only the ones listed in attrs. |
| `attrs` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Attribute labels to copy from the parent, used when mode is "specific". |
| `carrier` | str | `'dispose'` |  |  |  | "dispose": the batch ends here and its parts leave together. "keep": the batch is a carrier (a truck) that lives on -- its members leave one at a time by the first link, each after member_time, and the carrier leaves by the SECOND link once it is empty. |
| `member_time` | str | `''` |  | time | `member_time_unit` | Keep mode only: time for one member to come off, e.g. "2" or "TRIA(1, 2, 3)", evaluated for each member in its own scope when its turn starts. Empty = every member leaves in the same instant. |
| `member_time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit `member_time` is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `release_order` | str | `'fifo'` |  |  |  | Order the members leave in: "fifo" (the order they were loaded) or "lifo" (last loaded first off, a rear-door truck). |

Outputs: 1.

## SIGNAL

Broadcasts a named signal that releases every entity waiting at a HOLD block for it, for example a shift start, a gate opening or a green light. After an optional delay, succeeds the named signal event (releasing every HOLD block currently waiting on it) and immediately replaces it with a fresh one -- broadcast, edge-triggered, auto-reset.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `distribution` | str | `'Constant'` |  |  |  | Name of a registered distribution (see the distribution reference). |
| `dist_params` | dict | `{'value': 0.0}` |  | time | `time_unit` | Parameters for `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). |
| `time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit the sampled duration is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit, no conversion) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `signal_name` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of the signal to succeed; matches a HOLD block's signal_name. |

Outputs: 1.

## STATION

Named stop on a job-shop or multi-step routing where a ROUTE block delivers parts, orders or jobs and sets their current location. Named entry point of a routing. Entities arrive here from a ROUTE block whose sequence step names this block, or along an ordinary link; either way `entity.station` becomes this block's name and the entity continues along the station's single outgoing link.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `station` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Optional station name this block answers to, shown as `entity.station` and usable in a sequence step. Empty: the block's own name is the station name. |
| `node` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Optional path-network node this station sits on. With one, travel to and from this station is the shortest path along the network and `DISTANCE("...", "...")` can name it. |
| `tending` | dict | `{}` |  |  |  | Machine tending by a fleet with an `arm`: {"place": [segments], "pick": [segments], "time_unit": "seconds", "hrc": "none", "zone": {}, "cobot": "leave"|"stay"}. Segments, hrc and zone are a MOTION block's, timed with the fleet's arm profile; a missing cycle uses the fleet's flat unload/load time. The machine keeps a finished part until the cobot has picked it, and the cobot holds a part until the machine accepts it; "stay" keeps the cobot at the station until the part moves on. Empty: an ordinary station. |

Outputs: 1.

## SUBMODEL

Editor-only blocks (SUBMODEL, SUB_ENTRY, SUB_EXIT) that group blocks into a reusable sub-model with named ports, expanded away before the run. Editor-only placeholder shared by three types, never run directly -- `core/submodels.flatten()` expands them away before the engine builds any process. SUB_ENTRY: an input port of a submodel definition (`port` names it; exactly one outgoing link inside the definition, none incoming). SUB_EXIT: an output port of a definition (`port` names it; incoming links only). SUBMODEL: an instance of a definition dropped on the canvas (`definition` names it, `arguments` binds its parameters).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `definition` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of the submodel definition |
| `arguments` | dict | `{}` |  |  |  | Parameter bindings: {name: number | expression | bool} |
| `preset` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Provenance only: the catalogue row whose values were written into `arguments`. The values are what the model uses, so editing one afterwards is fine and nothing re-reads the catalogue. |

Outputs: multiple, chosen at run time.

## TRANSFER

Adds to or takes from a continuous tank, stock or inventory level (fuel, material, a pool) as the entity passes, optionally waiting until it is available.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | str | `''` | yes |  |  | Name of the level this block adds to or removes from. |
| `amount` | str | `'1'` |  |  |  | How much to move: an expression, e.g. 20 or entity.quantity. |
| `mode` | str | `'remove'` |  |  |  | "remove" takes the amount out of the level, "add" puts it in. |
| `wait` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | Wait until the level can pay the full amount (the backorder pattern); otherwise move what it can and record the rest as unmet. |

Outputs: 1.

## TRANSPORT

Moves a part, order or load between locations with a vehicle (truck, AGV, forklift, robot) from a fleet: fetch, carry, unload, free the vehicle.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fleet` | str | `''` | yes |  |  | Name of the mover fleet whose vehicles do the carrying. |
| `destination` | str | `''` |  |  |  | STATION the entity is carried to. Empty: the next station of the entity's routing, exactly as ROUTE would choose it. |
| `priority` | int | `0` |  |  |  | Request priority for a vehicle; lower is served first, and outranks the fleet's dispatching rule. |
| `keep_vehicle` | bool | `False` |  |  |  | Keep the vehicle after the drop: it waits there, busy, and the entity's next TRANSPORT on this fleet drives it. A RELEASE naming the fleet, or the entity leaving the model, frees it. |

Outputs: 1.
